title: The Hidden Cost of Buy Now, Pay Later
summary: Former CFPB director Rohit Chopra explains BNPL's hidden costs, data practices, and the rollback of federal oversight.

assertions.quote: about a quarter of Buy Now, Pay Later borrowers say they've used it for groceries
58% of borrowers say they used it because it was the only way they could afford their purchases
retailers pay just about 3% of the purchase price to accept our credit card, they often pay 6% or more
some charge late fees as high as 25% of the total loan

verdicts.note: Several providers' published fee schedules include late fees that can run into a substantial percentage of smaller loan amounts.
KC Fed endnote: several BNPL providers, including Afterpay and Klarna, charge a late fee up to 25% of the total purchase amount or a fixed amount.

assertions.quote: some lenders track our precise geolocation, our interactions with apps on our devices, and even our web browsing history

verdicts.note: Consistent with providers' own privacy policies describing use of location, app, and browsing data, though the degree varies by lender.

CFPB: BNPL lenders 'deploy models, product features, and marketing campaigns' based on collected demographic, psychographic, and behavioral data to decide which products and brands are promoted to each consumer.

assertions.quote: Buy Now, Pay Later companies lobbied to get it killed, and the Trump administration dutifully complied
